headline: SIPRI examined the military AI industry's obligations under humanitarian law, as Helsing unveiled interceptor missiles against Russian drones and Anthropic's IPO filing disclosed extraordinary AI existential-risk warnings.

points.text: SIPRI published a backgrounder on the military AI industry's involvement in armed conflict and how international humanitarian law applies to it.
Germany's Helsing unveiled interceptor missiles with AI software to organize intercepts of Russia's fast-flying Geran attack drones, priced under $100,000 per shot.
CSET overviewed how black-box distillation works in practice, informing proposed legislation and policy debates on adversarial distillation from proprietary US AI models.
Anthropic filed its S-1 prospectus with the SEC ahead of its IPO, disclosing an extensive list of extreme risk factors including the chance its own technology could endanger humanity.
Google released Gemini 4 Argon with a compact 14-page model card alongside a much longer, 217-page safety and security report.
Axios reported that Meta's $42 billion in recent legal penalties and settlements is a warning to AI companies that courts could catch up with them even as regulation lags.
